viewer_sees: A Greek musician, a Japanese god and a file of seven Cherokee men walk one behind the other across a grey dusk plain, left to right, toward one vast black gap in a cliff at the right edge
The musician, now close, walks on alone toward the black opening as the god and the file of men fall back out of frame
Orpheus plays the lyre in a sunlit meadow, boulders and oaks leaning toward the sound; Eurydice stops mid-dance and looks down as a snake slips away through the grass
Orpheus plays before the thrones of the king and queen of the dead in a black cavern hall; their stern faces soften as the shades lean toward him
Orpheus climbs a rising path of loose black stone toward a small disc of daylight at the left, Eurydice's pale shade following several steps behind him
At the cave mouth, bright daylight beyond, Orpheus turns his head; Eurydice's reaching hand loses its colour and she is drawn back into the grey mist
An open scroll of old paper and a brush on a low dark desk beside a small paper lamp, brush strokes of script, no readable text
Izanagi walks down a dark earthen passage toward a heavy timber door with a red-black glow leaking from under it
At the door, Izanagi reaches toward a tall dark figure in the doorway whose face is lost in shadow; she shakes her head slowly and lifts a bowl from the hearth beside her
She raises a hand to warn him off, turns and walks back into the dark hall, the heavy door swinging shut on her; Izanagi stands alone at the threshold
Izanagi waits at the shut door, then breaks a tooth from the comb in his hair, lights it, and pushes the door open with the small flame held up
Torchlight falls on Izanami in the dark hall: her wasted grey form half in shadow, pale specks crawling over her robe, eight small coiling shapes of storm cloud and lightning gathered about her
Izanagi runs out through the hall toward the light at the left; behind him a dark host of the dead with pale faces pours after him
Running up the passage, Izanagi flings his black headdress behind him and grapes burst across the floor; he flings his comb and bamboo shoots spring up; the pursuers stop to eat
At the foot of the pass Izanagi throws three peaches and the host of the dead scatters; Izanami's great dark form rises out of the gloom at the right
Izanagi heaves a rock the size of a house into the narrow pass until it seals the way; dust and grit pour down the banks
LEDGER/ACCUMULATION: Izanami at the right side of the sealed rock speaks across it; far below at the left a field of a thousand small lamps goes out row by row
LEDGER/ACCUMULATION: Izanagi at the left side of the rock answers across it; far below at the left rows of new thatched huts rise and light up warm one after another
TIMELINE: one fixed view of a Japanese village from dusk to dawn; a quiet funeral line with lanterns leaves at the left while a birth-hut door opens warm and gold at the right and the sun rises
Dawn over a southern Appalachian valley: blue ridges, mist on the river, smoke rising from a Cherokee town of round bark houses and a domed council house
The Sun, a vast woman of burning light, pours heat down toward the tiny wilting earth; at the right her daughter stands in the doorway of a house in the sky and a rattlesnake strikes
The Sun covers her face and weeps; her light drains out of the sky and the valley below goes dark
In the dark valley, seven Cherokee men with long sourwood rods set out single file along a ridge trail toward the west, carrying a box between them
In the Ghost country the dead dance in a ring round a low fire; as the Sun's daughter passes the nearest man he touches her with his rod and she sinks to the ground beside the open box
The seven men carry the closed box east along the ridge trail at first light; a man presses his hand flat on the lid and warns the others; the lid shivers from inside
The men halt in the thicket; the box knocks and a man leans his ear to it; at last he lifts the lid a hand's breadth
A small red bird bursts out of the lifted lid past the men's faces and darts into the thicket
In the town the men open the box before the council house and find it empty; they stand with the rods hanging from their hands
MACRO OBJECT: on one worn black slab by firelight lie a broken comb, a tortoise-shell lyre and a cane-splint box, left to right in the order of the three rules
Close on the comb at the left of the slab: one tooth has been broken off and its tip burns with a small flame that leans and flares
The view drifts right across the lyre, its strings trembling, to the box, whose lid lifts a finger's width and lets out a thin line of light
ANIMATED MAP: an old parchment map of the northern world, small lights flickering on across North America, and a question mark of mist over the whole
A line of small figures in furs crosses a vast pale ice-age plain at dawn, left to right, mist blowing across their path
A medicine man sits in a dim bark lodge drumming by a low fire, eyes closed; the smoke rises and draws out into a pale path leading away into the dark
SILHOUETTE: a dark night land with three small fires far apart, each with one dark figure beside it, under the same turning stars
Close on one cloaked mourner at the edge of a small fire, face lifted to the night sky, breath rising pale in the cold
The seven men sit in the dusk before the council house around the empty box; one of them slowly closes the lid, and a redbird watches from a branch above
EMPTY AFTERMATH: the empty box on the packed earth at the edge of the town, lid open, ash of a cold fire beside it, the redbird gone from the branch
The same plain at pale dawn: three small figures walk back out of the black gap, right to left toward the light, each empty-handed: a limp lyre, a burnt-out comb stub, an open empty box
End card: a poster of the whole story with the title, the three travellers and the SUBSCRIBE button
